summary: Updates RFC 3967 so the IESG has more flexibility in accepting downward references, where a Standards Track document refers to a lower maturity document, without needing explicit mention in the Last Call. It is a BCP.

plainLanguage.summary: This Best Current Practice updates the process for normative references to documents at a lower maturity level. It makes explicit mention during Last Call strongly recommended rather than required.

subtitle: A Best Current Practice update that gives the IESG more flexibility when reviewing downrefs.

tldr.problem: RFC 3967 required downrefs to be explicitly identified in the IETF Last Call, and missing one could lead to repeating the Last Call.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8067 makes identifying downrefs in the Last Call strongly recommended but not required, leaving repeat decisions to the IESG.
tldr.outcome: The rest of the RFC 3967 process remains in effect, and the IESG considers whether to consult the community again on a case-by-case basis.

today: RFC 8067 is a Best Current Practice that updates RFC 3967. The unit metadata lists no RFC that updates or obsoletes RFC 8067.

sections.title: The Downref Process
sections.content:
A normative reference is one a document relies on as part of its requirements. RFC 3967 describes how a Standards Track or Best Current Practice document can refer normatively to a document at a lower maturity level, a practice called a downref.

The earlier process required the need for a downref to be called out in the IETF Last Call. RFC 8067 says this requirement proved unnecessarily restrictive and sometimes caused a Last Call to be repeated without real benefit.
sections.plainLanguage: A standards document may rely on a document at a lower maturity level. The previous process required that this be called out during Last Call.

sections.title: IESG Review of Downrefs
sections.content:
Explicitly documenting downrefs in the Last Call is now strongly recommended, but it is not required. The responsible Area Director should still check for downrefs before sending the notice.

If a downref is found during Last Call or IESG review, the IESG decides whether to repeat Last Call. If it does not, the downref's maturity status does not change, and RFC 3967 still applies if the downref is used in the future. The responsible Area Director should record an omission in the datatracker.
sections.plainLanguage: The Area Director should check for downrefs before Last Call. If one is found late, the IESG decides whether the community needs another review.

sections.title: Security and Stability
sections.content: The RFC notes that references to immature protocols can have security and stability implications. The IESG should consider those implications when deciding whether another community consultation is useful.
sections.plainLanguage: A less mature protocol can raise security or stability concerns. The IESG should consider those risks when deciding whether to ask for more review.

references.text: Bush, R. and T. Narten, "Clarifying when Standards Track Documents may Refer Normatively to Documents at a Lower Level", BCP 97, RFC 3967, December 2004.
